channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Eleição de 2026 deve ter menor número de debates de TV no 1º turno em 28 anos
item.description: The 2026 presidential election is expected to have the lowest number of televised debates in the first round since 1998, with only Band, in partnership with Estadão, having conducted debates among candidates for the Presidency. The reduction in public debate may affect transparency and the depth of electoral proposals.

item.title: Governo Lula anuncia proibição das bets no Brasil e propõe prisão para operadores
item.description: The Lula government announced the banning of sports betting and online casino games in Brazil, as part of a new economic package focused on fighting over-indebtedness and social protection. The measure aims to reduce financial losses for the population and strengthen public policies.

item.title: André Mendonça vota para absolver Eduardo Bolsonaro por acusação de difamação contra Tabata
item.description: Minister André Mendonça voted to acquit Eduardo Bolsonaro on a defamation charge against Tabata Amaral, arguing his statements are protected by parliamentary immunity. However, the majority voted to convict with a one-year prison sentence, though implementation remains undefined. The trial is taking place in the STF's virtual plenary and concludes on Friday.

item.title: Bets cogitam ir à Justiça e cobrar até dano moral de Lula: 'Setor não vai acabar amanhã'
item.description: Lula and team members consider filing a lawsuit against the legalization of online betting, citing risks to the economy and public security. The National Games and Lotteries Association claims the regulated market generates jobs and tax revenue.

item.title: Lula anuncia proibição das bets no Brasil: entenda a medida e até quando apostadores poderão sacar dinheiro
item.description: The federal government announced a provisional measure to ban online betting platforms in Brazil, known as 'bets'. Users will have until October 5th to withdraw their balances, and from October 6th onward, the platforms will be blocked. The ban was announced nine days before the first round of the 2026 elections, a time when the government seeks to improve its standing in voter intention polls.

item.title: Em agenda no DF, Michelle pede pacificação: "Não vamos brigar com lulistas"
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro (PL) and Celina Leão (PP) held a campaign parade in Vila Planalto, DF, where Michelle called for calm by avoiding confrontations with Lula supporters, emphasizing a respectful tone. The Senate candidate also criticized aggressive protesters and stressed the importance of dialogue between political opponents.

item.title: 'Proibir não é proteger': associações se posicionam contra a MP de Lula que proíbe bets no Brasil
item.description: The federal government announced a ban on sports betting in Brazil through a Provisional Measure, which also criminalizes unauthorized betting operations and promotion. Industry associations criticized the measure, arguing that prohibition may drive bettors to illegal offshore sites lacking oversight or consumer protections. Instead of banning, the associations advocate for stronger regulation, deposit and time limits, stricter advertising rules, and crackdowns on unlicensed operators.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz que ‘Lula tenta fazer estelionato antes da eleição’ ao proibir bets no País
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro harshly criticized the Lula government over a provisional decree banning sports betting (bets) in the country, accusing him of electoral fraud and opportunism. He pointed out that it was Lula who legalized bets and is now trying to eliminate them for political gain ahead of the elections. The PL candidate also promised to ban online casinos and platforms like Tigrinho.

item.title: José Sarney continua internado em hospital em SP e tem previsão de alta para a próxima semana
item.description: Former President José Sarney, 96, remains hospitalized at Sírio-Libanês Hospital in São Paulo, with expected discharge next week following pneumonia treatment. His daughter Roseana Sarney is running for the Federal Senate by MDB-MA.

item.title: Estudo do NetLab indica que Kwai descumpre regras do TSE sobre anúncios eleitorais
item.description: A NetLab study indicates that Kwai does not fully comply with TSE regulations regarding electoral ads, hindering the oversight of paid advertisements. The platform fails to accurately report spending, does not provide the profile of the reached audience, and limits data collection. NetLab plans to submit the report to TSE, which is already reviewing the content.

item.title: Mendonça mandar derrubar posts sobre falso apoio de Flávio a tirar ‘padroeira’ de N. S. Aparecida
item.description: Minister André Mendonça of the STF ordered the removal of 1,125 social media posts that falsely linked Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to a bill seeking to strip Nossa Senhora Aparecida of her status as Brazil’s patron saint. Left-wing profiles spread the claim that evangelicals supported removing the Catholic saint as national patroness, triggering 2.3 million interactions across major digital platforms in under 18 hours.

item.title: A aposta da campanha de Lula com a proibição das bets na reta final do primeiro turno
item.description: Lula announced the ban on sports betting and online casinos via provisional decree, linking the issue to household debt and gambling addiction. The campaign assesses that the anti-bets offensive has broad support, especially in the final stretch of the first round, aiming to consolidate this stance as a political differentiator.

item.title: Governo proíbe apostas e publicidade de bets no país, e plataformas sairão do ar
item.description: The federal government announced a complete ban on online betting in Brazil, immediately blocking new bets, deposits, and advertising, with full shutdown of websites and apps on October 6th. Users have until October 5th to withdraw balances, after the first round of elections. The measure, issued as a provisional decree, must be approved by Congress within 120 days to remain in effect.

item.title: Bets têm até o dia 5/10 para devolver dinheiro de apostadores
item.description: President Lula signed a provisional measure prohibiting online betting in Brazil, requiring platforms to return funds to bettors by October 5, with website blocking starting October 6. The measure also establishes specific crimes for the sector, bans betting advertisements, and creates a debt renegotiation program for those indebted due to gambling addiction.

item.title: Quaest em AL: Lula, 44%; Flávio Bolsonaro, 32%
item.description: A Quaest survey released on September 25, 2026 shows Lula leading the presidential race in Alagoas with 44%, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 32% in the projected first-round results. The poll interviewed 804 people between September 21 and 24, with a margin of error of 3 percentage points.

item.title: Datafolha em PE: Lula, 60%; Flávio Bolsonaro, 24%; Cury, 3%; Renan, 2%; Caiado, 2%
item.description: The Datafolha poll in Pernambuco shows Lula leading with 60%, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 24%. The runoff simulation indicates a Lula victory over Flávio, while the government's approval rating stands at 64%.

item.title: Governo federal arrecadou R$ 15,3 bilhões com bets desde o início de 2025
item.description: The federal government collected R$ 15.3 billion from betting company taxation since early 2025, helping meet fiscal targets. This week, a ban on online betting and virtual games was announced, with the tax rate expected to reach 18% by 2028.

item.title: Datafolha no RJ: Flávio Bolsonaro, 44%; Lula, 38%; Cury, Renan e Caiado, 3%
item.description: A Datafolba poll released in Rio de Janeiro shows Flávio Bolsonaro leading with 44% and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva with 38% in the first-round simulation. In the second-round scenario, Flávio maintains an advantage with 51% against Lula's 42%. The poll was commissioned by Globo and Folha de S.Paulo with a 3-point margin of error.

item.title: Datafolha em SP: Flávio Bolsonaro, 38%; Lula, 33%; Cury, 7%; Caiado, 5%; Renan, 4%; Zema, 2%
item.description: Datafolha poll in São Paulo shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading with 38%, followed by Lula (PT) at 33% in the 2026 presidential race. In a simulated second round, Flávio rises to 49% against Lula's 41%.

item.title: Vetadas por Lula, bets foram legalizadas em 2018 e regulamentadas em 2023; veja o histórico
item.description: Sports betting was legalized in 2018 under President Temer, even though it was not originally included in the bill sent to Congress. Regulation only took place in 2023, during Lula's third term, following public consultations started under Bolsonaro's administration.

item.title: Datafolha no DF: Flávio, 41%; Lula, 34%; Caiado; 9%; Cury, 4%; Renan, 3%; Zema, 1%
item.description: Datafolha, commissioned by Globo and Folha, shows Flávio Bolsonaro leading with 41% and Lula with 34% among DF voters. In a simulated runoff, Lula leads with 51% against Flávio's 41%. The survey also reveals 56% disapproval of the federal government.

item.title: Datafolha em MG: Lula, 39%; Flávio Bolsonaro, 37%; Cury, 5%; Zema, 4%; Caiado, 3%
item.description: Datafolha polling in Minas Gerais shows Lula (PT) at 39% and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) at 37% in the first round, effectively tied within the margin of error. In the second round simulation, Flávio leads 46% to 44%. Government approval in MG is split, with 51% disapproving and 46% approving.

item.title: Mendonça manda derrubar até memes sobre Flávio Bolsonaro e Nossa Senhora
item.description: TSE Minister André Mendonça ordered the removal of posts falsely claiming Flávio Bolsonaro or relatives intend to strip Nossa Senhora Aparecida of her status as Brazil's patron saint, expanding prior measures targeting Antonio Tabet. The ruling covers social media content, including memes and substantively equivalent reproductions, following widespread multiplatform replication and over 2,000 flagged posts. The measure aims to curb election-related disinformation involving religious and political figures.

item.title: Quanto os brasileiros deixam nas bets? Estudo estimou R$ 62,5 bilhões em 2025, mas o setor contesta
item.description: The federal government announced a ban on online betting and virtual game platforms, with a bill to be sent to Congress establishing penalties for those who exploit, operate, or advertise betting sites. A Comsefaz study estimated that online bets drained R$62.5 billion from Brazilian families' budgets in 2025, equivalent to 0.68% of disposable income, raising concerns about households' ability to meet financial obligations. The industry disputes the data and warns of the low economic multiplier effect of transactions conducted via PIX.

item.title: Governo Lula anuncia proibição de bets no Brasil a 9 dias da eleição
item.description: President Lula banned online betting in Brazil nine days before the election, setting a deadline for balance withdrawals until October 5th and automatic refunds after October 14th. The measure aims to combat gambling addiction but raises debates about economic freedom.

item.title: Flávio celebra decisão de Mendonça contra “fake news” sobre Nossa Senhora Aparecida
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro praised Minister André Mendonça's decision from the TSE ordering the removal of posts containing fake news linking him to Our Lady of Aparecida. The PL candidate hailed the ruling as a victory against disinformation.

item.title: Datafolha: Flávio Bolsonaro lidera em SP e RJ, Lula fica à frente em PE, e MG tem empate
item.description: The Datafolha survey shows a tie between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in Minas Gerais, while Flávio leads in São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, and Lula is ahead in Pernambuco.

item.title: Bap rebate Lula sobre bets: “Não temos que aprender nada”
item.description: Luiz Eduardo Baptista (Bap), president of Flamengo, pushed back on President Lula's remarks about football clubs' reliance on betting revenues, stating the club operates within legality and has nothing to learn. He emphasized that regulated betting generates over R$400 million for Flamengo and moves R$2.5 billion in Brazilian football, arguing that banning legal activities does not eliminate consumption but merely pushes betters to illegal platforms.

item.title: A 9 dias das eleições, governo anuncia proibição de bets no Brasil
item.description: The federal government announced, nine days before the elections, the ban on online betting and games in Brazil, which will be formalized through a Provisional Measure and a bill. Bettors will have until October 5th to withdraw balances, after which the sites will be shut down and banks will return the funds.

item.title: Dani Lima: Campanha de Flávio assume desgaste e elo com ex-sócio de Vorcaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) campaign faces backlash after revelations that he returned from the US on a plane owned by Daniel Vorcaro and lawyer Willer Tomaz. Daniela Lima highlighted the negative impact of this connection with controversial figures on the 'Pulso Político' show.

item.title: PSOL pede investigação de Bia Kicis após investigado da PF fazer publicidade com nome Bia
item.description: The Socialism and Liberty Party (PSOL) requested the Supreme Federal Court to investigate an amendment of R$250,000 allocated by federal deputy Bia Kicis to the Viver-Brasil Institute, an entity linked to an individual investigated for ties to the film 'Dark Horse'. Kicis, running for the Senate under PL-DF, faces allegations of misuse of public funds.

item.title: Alckmin diz que Lula preservará tradições católicas em meio à polêmica sobre Nossa Senhora Aparecida
item.description: Vice-president Geraldo Alckmin stated that the Lula administration will protect Brazilian Catholic traditions amid controversy over an alleged initiative to remove the title of patron saint of Brazil from Our Lady of Aparecida. The controversy emerged after social media posts linked Flávio Bolsonaro to a bill archived in 2008, which he denied. Alckmin emphasized respect for all religions.

item.title: Boulos se licencia da Secretaria Geral para auxiliar campanha de Lula
item.description: Minister Guilherme Boulos (Psol-SP) will step away from the Secretariat-General of the Presidency to support Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's (PT) reelection campaign, with the role temporarily assumed by executive secretary Josué Augusto do Amaral Rocha. The leave, to be published in the Official Gazette on Monday (Sept 28), takes effect six days before the first round on Oct 4 and will be unpaid. Boulos had already been actively campaigning, attending public events and posting on social media, mirroring the strategy used by other government ministers like Luiz Marinho (PT-SP).

item.title: Felipe Roth detalha propostas de Renan Santos para a saúde
item.description: Felipe Roth, health coordinator for Renan Santos's campaign, detailed proposals such as SUS Fila Zero, prioritizing care by clinical severity, and the hub and spoke model for complex cases. He also discussed unlinking the constitutional floors for health and education from federal revenue through a PEC by Kim Kataguiri, and highlighted the absence of a childhood vaccination goal in the government plan.

item.title: Lucas Pavanato é condenado a indenizar a estudante da PUC por vídeo
item.description: Vereador Lucas Pavanato (PL-SP) was ordered to compensate a PUC-SP student for R$7,500 after sharing a video recorded without her consent during a university event in 2022. Judge Airtom Marquezini Júnior deemed the action unlawful following the revocation of consent for image use and mandated removal of the post. The ruling highlights ongoing debates around digital rights and personal data protection in Brazil.

item.title: Fachin manda PGR analisar pendências nos casos Master e INSS
item.description: Supreme Court President Edson Fachin ordered the Attorney General's Office (PGR) to review pending issues in the Master and INSS cases, assessing the relevance and impact of requested measures on ongoing investigations. The PGR has five days to submit an opinion, which will be sent to the STF. The decision follows the suspension of inquiries at the Presidency and the disclosure of messages between Moraes and the founder of Banco Master.

item.title: Lula enfim vai a Pernambuco pedir votos para João Campos
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) traveled to Pernambuco to publicly support João Campos (PSB), the candidate seeking re-election as state governor. The visit, which included First Lady Janja, marked a strategic alignment between national and local political leaders, reinforcing Campos' campaign with direct support from a key national figure. Polls show Campos in second place, just behind the incumbent governor, as both compete in an election seen as pivotal for regional political dynamics.

item.title: ‘Injustiça’, diz Deltan Dallagnol sobre proibição de fazer campanha mesmo com candidatura mantida
item.description: Deltan Dallagnol denounces what he calls an injustice regarding his Senate candidacy: his registration is upheld, yet he remains barred from campaigning following conflicting rulings by the Paraná Electoral Court and the Superior Electoral Court. He criticizes the judiciary for allegedly applying the law selectively against former Lava Jato members. Despite the ban, he claims his polling numbers have risen due to organic online support.

item.title: Fake news sobre Flávio e Nossa Senhora Aparecida circula entre católicos
item.description: False fake news circulated among Catholics claiming Flávio Bolsonaro intended to remove Our Lady of Aparecida's status as Brazil's patron saint. No such proposal exists from the candidate. The misinformation spread quickly through social media and WhatsApp groups.

item.title: Garotinho desmente rumores de que abandonou eleição no Rio
item.description: Former Rio de Janeiro governor Anthony Garotinho (Republicanos) denied rumors of withdrawing from the state gubernatorial race, stating in a live stream that 'he is a candidate and never considered quitting'. His candidacy registration was rejected by the Rio Electoral Court (TRE-RJ), and he awaits a ruling on appeals at the Supreme Electoral Court (TSE). The judicial outcome could significantly influence the direction of the state election.

item.title: Alckmin comenta polêmica envolvendo Nossa Senhora Aparecida e Flávio
item.description: Vice President Geraldo Alckmin (PSB) commented on a false controversy involving Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and an alleged removal of Our Lady of Aparecida's title as Brazil's patron saint. Alckmin stated that while President Lula is in office, religious traditions will be protected. Flávio strongly denied the accusations, calling them lies and attributing the campaign to the PT.

item.title: BH tem urnas para eleitor treinar voto antes das eleições; veja locais
item.description: The TRE-MG provides voting simulation booths in Belo Horizonte for citizens to practice before the October 4th election, with both in-person sessions and an online simulator available via the TSE website.

item.title: Medida de Lula contra bets é “hipócrita e eleitoreira”, diz Flávio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro accuses Lula of hypocrisy for banning online betting before elections, calling it populist and politically motivated. The measure will be announced in São Paulo, 10 days before the first round. Flávio promises to veto online casinos if elected but does not clarify his stance on sports betting platforms.

item.title: Lula proibir bets é 'desespero por votos' e pode ter impacto em eleição apertada, afirma professor da USP
item.description: President Lula announces the ban on online betting platforms ('bets') nine days before the first round, a measure with strong popular appeal (75% in favor) but whose electoral impact remains uncertain in a tight race against Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Lula promulga acordo de livre comércio entre Mercosul e EFTA
item.description: President Lula promulgated the free trade agreement between Mercosul and EFTA, effective October 2026, aiming to reduce trade barriers and expand market access. The treaty includes customs facilitation, investment rules and cooperation on intellectual property and sustainable development.

item.title: Pablo Marçal é condenado a pagar R$ 10 mil por soprar farinha no rosto de candidato em 2024
item.description: Former coach Pablo Marçal was ordered to pay R$10,000 in moral damages to candidate Marco Antonio Mills Martins after posting a video in which he throws flour in his face and associates him with drug use. The ruling was issued by the 1st Civil and Criminal Special Court of Barueri, based on a post that garnered over 7 million views.

item.title: Deltan diz ter sido “calado” no TSE por “indicado por Lula e melhor amigo de Moraes”
item.description: The Senate candidate from Paraná, Deltan Dallganol (Novo), claimed his campaign was suspended by TSE minister Floriano de Azevedo Marques, whom he accuses of being indicated by Lula and a friend of Moraes. He questions the impartiality of the judicial decision.

item.title: TJ-SP condena Pablo Marçal a pagar R$ 10 mil por danos morais a dirigente da Rede
item.description: The São Paulo State Court sentenced Pablo Marçal to pay R$ 10,000 in moral damages to Rede leader Marco Martins after the influencer sprinkled flour on his face and shared the video with derogatory captions online. The ruling, issued at first instance, emphasized the aggressive and defamatory nature of the act, which exceeded 7 million views. The decision can be appealed within 10 days.

item.title: Áudio: Estabilidade para grávida em contrato temporário vai a nova votação na CAS
item.description: The Senate's Social Affairs Committee is set to vote in a supplementary round on PL 3.522/2025, which establishes job stability for pregnant women under temporary contracts. The worker will be protected from pregnancy confirmation until five months after childbirth, based on decisions by the Supreme Federal Court and the Superior Labor Court. The text is expected to move forward as an advancement of rights for pregnant workers.

item.title: Lindbergh aciona STF contra Flávio e Willer por esquema na Loterj
item.description: Lindbergh Farias filed a petition with the STF requesting investigation into an alleged money laundering scheme involving Flávio Bolsonaro and Willer Tomaz at Loterj. The accusation indicates that Willer controlled RioPag through front companies, diverting over R$20.9 million in public funds.
